city_center.name: Downtown Oklahoma City / Stockyards City
city_center.landmark: Stockyards City along Exchange Avenue -- a working livestock market since 1910 with classic red-brick architecture; Route 66 threads 51.5 miles through the city
city_center.notes: Oklahoma City's first major industry was livestock: stockyards and meat-packing opened in 1910, and Stockyards City on Exchange Avenue still runs live cattle auctions. Route 66 (centennial 2026) crosses the city with neon and art-deco stretches. sources: Oklahoma National Stockyards (okhistory.org); Stockyards City (retrometrookc.org, travelok.com); OKC Route 66 (nationalgeographic.com).

cultural_notes: livestock marketing was Oklahoma City's first major industry -- stockyards and meat-packing plants opened in 1910, and Stockyards City on Exchange Avenue is still a working livestock market with Monday and Tuesday cattle auctions and classic red-brick architecture (source: okhistory.org Oklahoma National Stockyards; travelok.com Stockyards City; retrometrookc.org)

Route 66 runs 51.5 miles through Oklahoma City -- the highway marks its centennial in 2026 -- known for murals, neon-sign neighborhoods, and art-deco architecture (source: nationalgeographic.com OKC Route 66 guide)

Homeland is a locally owned, employee-owned Oklahoma grocery chain that leans hard on neighborhood identity ('Welcome Friends, Locally Owned -- Community Proud'), including a northeast-OKC store celebrating Black history through public art (source: okcretail.com Homeland; freep.com Homeland mural)

central Oklahoma sits on the red-earth Southern Plains, where iron-rich soil gives the ground and dust a distinctive red cast -- a regional landscape-color signature (INFERRED landscape-color framing from region knowledge -- verify before production use)
